name: @gnoverse/x402-gno
description: The gno payment mechanism for the x402 'exact' scheme. Register it on a stock x402 client and it signs payments for the gno chain an offer names.
//repository: npm resolves the package page's relative links against this, and the published page is the repository root README rather than client/README.md.
//bin: x402-gno is the weather buyer, so `npx github:gnoverse/x402#<ref> <seller URL>` pays a seller without a clone, and the published package carries the same command. npm installs only the package at a repository's root, which is why the command is declared here and its file is listed in `files`.
//exports: The subpath is the ecosystem's own grid — @x402/evm publishes ./exact/client, ./exact/server and ./exact/facilitator, so a buyer that already imports one reaches for the same path here. gno's server half is Go, so ./exact/client is the only cell this package fills.
//publishConfig: The registry is pinned so a publish cannot be redirected by an .npmrc or a stray environment variable, matching @gnolang/gno-js-client. access is public because scoped packages default to private.
//engines: The floor a CONSUMER needs, not the one this repo builds with: the emit targets ES2023, which Node 20 covers in full, and neither @gnolang runtime dependency declares a constraint of its own. Working on the package needs newer — tsdown wants Node ^22.18.0 or >=24.11.0, and CI runs 24.
//scripts: prepublishOnly runs on every publish, from CI or a laptop. `files` ships client/dist, so publishing an unbuilt tree would put a package on the registry whose single export path does not resolve — and a burned version number can never be reused. prepare builds that tree when npm installs the package from git, as npx github:… does: client/dist is not committed, and the x402-gno command imports it. npm also runs prepare after npm install or npm ci in a clone, unless scripts are ignored.
//dependencies: Versions are exact so a signed payment changes only when a dependency is deliberately bumped. @x402/core is a peer: the mechanism uses only its types and the x402-gno command its stock client, and neither may pull in a second copy of the client a consumer already has. @cosmjs/crypto, which the command draws a new key's mnemonic with, is the version @gnolang/tm2-js-client pins, so it adds nothing to an install.
//peerDependencies: 2.23 is the first @x402/core with setSpendControls. From that version a stock client pays only in USD-pegged assets unless they are listed there, and ugnot is not one, so every buyer of this mechanism calls it.
